sentences.text: JUDGMENT

This is petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, seeking compensation of Rs.65,00,000/- from the respondents on account of death of Sandanu A. S., who is son of petitioners No.1 and 2 and brother of petitioner No.3, in a road traffic accident.

2. The brief facts of the case are as follows:
On 30-06-2023 at about 1.30 a.m., deceased Sandanu A. S., was riding the motorcycle bearing No. KL-21-W-7467 from Bengaluru towards Nelamangala, near Makali Bus-stand, Bengaluru-Tumkur NH-48 Road, Bengaluru District.

At that time,
the driver of truck bearing Reg. No. MH-12-MV-1905 came from Bengaluru towards Nelamangala, in rash and negligent manner, from right side to left side and dashed to the motorcycle of the deceased Sandanu A. S.
Due to said impact, the deceased sustained grievous injuries all over the body and succumbed to injuries while shifting to Confido Hospital at Bengaluru.
Earlier to the accident, the deceased was doing business and was earning a sum of Rs.30,000/- per month.
He was contributing his entire earnings to his family.
Due to untimely death of a sole bread earner, the petitioners are struggling for their livelihood.
The Nelamangala Traffic Police have registered the case against the driver of the said truck for the offences punishable under Section 279 and 304(A) of I.P.C.
The respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
Hence, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
Therefore, it is prayed to allow the petition and award compensation of Rs.65,00,000/- with interest.
3. On service of notice to the respondents, the respondent No.2 appeared through its counsel and filed the written statement.
Whereas, the respondent No.1 did not chose to appear and remained absent.
Hence, the respondent No.1 is placed as ex-parte.

4. The respondent No.2 in its written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition.
It has admitted the issuance of insurance policy in respect of truck bearing No. MH-12-MV-1905 and its validity as on the date of accident.
It has specifically contended that, the driver of the truck bearing No. MH-12-MV-1905 was not having valid driving licence to drive the said truck.

The investigation officer has filed charge-sheet against the owner of said vehicle under Section 180 of Motor Vehicles Act, for allowing the driver to drive the said vehicle without having valid driving licence and also against the driver under Section 181 of Motor Vehicles Act, for driving the said truck without having valid driving licence and also under Section 304(A), 279 of I.P.C.
It seeks protection under Section 147 and 149(2) of Motor Vehicles Act.
It has contended that, the petition is bad for non compliance of provision under Sections 134(c) and 158(6) of Motor Vehicles Act.
It has denied the age, avocation and income of the deceased.
It is further contended that, the compensation claimed is highly excessive and exaggerated.
Further, it sought for permission to contest even on behalf of respondent No.1 as per Section 170 of the Motor Vehicles Act.
In view of above denials and contentions, it prayed for dismissal of the petition.

5. On the basis of rival pleadings of both the sides, the following issues are framed:
ISSUES

2. Whether the petitioners are entitled to compensation? If so, what is the quantum and from whom ?

sentences.text: Issue No.1:

It is specific case of the petitioners that, on 30-06-2023 at about 1.30 a.m., deceased Sandanu A. S., was riding the motorcycle bearing No. KL-21-W-7467 from Bengaluru towards Nelamangala, near Makali Bus-stand, Bengaluru-Tumkur NH-48 Road, Bengaluru District.

Due to said impact, the deceased sustained grievous injuries all over the body and succumbed to injuries while shifting to Confido Hospital at Bengaluru.
10. In order to prove their case, the petitioner No.1 has got examined himself as P.W.1 by filing examination-in-chief affidavit and got marked total 18 documents as Ex.P.1 to 18.

Out of the said documents, Ex.P.1 is true copy of F.I.R., Ex.P.2 is true copy of first information statement, Ex.P.3 is true copy of Spot Mahazar, Ex.P.4 is true copy of seizure mahazar, Ex.P.5 is true copy of sketch,
Ex.P.6 is true copy of inquest, Ex.P.7 is true copy of postmortem report, Ex.P.8 is true copy of Section 133 M.V.A. notice, Ex.P.9 is true copy of reply to Section 133 M.V.A. notice, Ex.P.10 is true copy of M.V.A. report, Ex.P.11 is true copy of charge-sheet, Ex.P.12 to 16 are notarised copies of Aadhar cards (total 4), Ex.P.17 is notarised copy of driving licence and Ex.P.18 is notarised copy of score sheet.

11. At the outset, is it pertinent to note that, except the negligence of the driver of Truck bearing Reg.
No. MH-12- MV-1905, the date, time & place of accident, involvement of vehicles, death of Sandanu A.S., due to injuries caused in the accident, issuance of insurance policy and its validity are not in dispute.

On meticulously going through the police documents marked as Ex.P.1 to 11, prima-facia it reveals that, 30-06-2023 at about 1.30 a.m., deceased Sandanu A. S., along with pillion rider by name Rassal A. S/o Safamahal, was riding the motorcycle bearing No. KL-21-W-7467 from Bengaluru towards Nelamangala, near Makali Bus-stand, Bengaluru-Tumkur NH-48 Road,
Bengaluru District and they both were not wearing helmet.

At that time, the driver of offending truck bearing Reg. No. MH-12-MV-1905, without having valid driving licence to drive the said vehicle, came from Bengaluru towards Nelamangala side, in rash and negligent manner, from right side to left side and dashed to the motorcycle of the deceased Sandanu A. S.
Due to said impact, the deceased sustained grievous injuries all over the body and succumbed to injuries at Confido Hospital at Bengaluru.

The Ex.P.3 spot mahazer and Ex.P.5 sketch clearly speaks that, the alleged accident has taken place when the deceased was riding his motorcycle on extreme left side of 30 feet width Bengaluru-Tumkur NH-48 road.

The investigation officer in his final report has clearly stated that, on the alleged date, time and place of accident, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending Truck bearing Reg. No. MH-12-MV-1905 the said accident has taken place and the deceased Sandanu A.S., sustained grievous injuries all over the body and succumbed to said injuries when shifted to hospital.
There is absolutely no evidence placed on record by the respondents to rebut the final report of the investigation officer and other police documents produced by the petitioners.
12. The petitioner No.1, who has been examined as P.W.1, has reiterated the entire averments made in the petition.
The oral evidence of P.W.1 is fully corroborated with the documentary evidence marked as Ex.P.1 to 18.

Though, the learned counsel for respondent No.2 has cross-examined P.W.1 in length, nothing worth has been elicited from his mouth which creates doubt on the veracity of his Anilkumar G vs Nilesh Navale on 1 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/141366280/

Further, though, the respondent No.2 has specifically denied the above facts in his written statement, he has not produced any rebuttal evidence to disprove the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioners.

It is pertinent to note that, the P.W.1 has unequivocally denied the suggestion made by the learned counsel for respondent No.2 in his cross-examination that, the alleged accident has occurred due to rash and negligence driving of the deceased and not due to rash and negligent driving of the offending Truck bearing Reg. No. MH-12-MV-1905.

Further it is pertinent to note, as per Ex.P.10 Motor Vehicle Accident Report, the accident had not occurred due to any mechanical defects in the vehicles involved in the accident.

When the accident was not occurred due to the any mechanical defects in the offending vehicle and there was no negligence on the part of motorcycle rider, then it can be presumed that, the said accident had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle.

Further, the investigation officer has clearly stated in the final report, marked as Ex.P.11, that, the alleged accident has occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle bearing Reg. No.
MH-12-MV-1905.

There is absolutely no rebuttal evidence led by the respondents to disprove the case of the petitioners and even nothing is elicited in the cross-examination of P.W.1 to show that,
the alleged accident has occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the rider of motorcycle i.e.,
deceased and there is no negligence on the part of the driver of Truck bearing Reg. No.
MH-12-MV-1905.
Further, the Ex.P.7 Post-motem report, clearly speaks that, deceased Sandanu A.S., has died due to shock as a result of injury to major organs sustained in the motor vehicle accident.

In such circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the final report filed by the investigation officer and other police records, regarding the negligence of the driver of offending vehicle, place, date and time of accident, involvement of the offending vehicle and injuries caused to deceased Sandanu A.S., in the said accident.

15. Further, it is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims,
the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011)
SCC 635, has clearly held that, "in a road accident claim cases the strict principle of proof as in a criminal case are not required."

The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of National Insurance Co. V/s Birender, reported in (2020) 11 SCC 356, has clearly held that, "12.

sentences.text: The legal representatives of the deceased could move application for compensation by virtue of clause (c) of Section 166(1).
The major married son who is also earning and not fully dependant on the deceased, would be still covered by the expression "legal representative" of the deceased.
This Court in Manjuri Bera (supra) had expounded that liability to pay compensation under the Act does not cease because of absence of dependency of the concerned legal representative.
Notably, the expression "legal representative" has not been defined in the Act.
10. The Tribunal has a duty to make an award, determine the amount of compensation which is just and proper and specify the person or persons to whom such compensation would be paid.
The latter part relates to the entitlement of compensation by a person who claims for the same.

11. According to Section 2(11) CPC, "legal representative" means a person who in law represents the Tractor and Trally bearing No.AP-03-AN-8690 & AP-03-AN-8712 estate of a deceased person, and includes any person who intermeddles with the estate of the deceased and where a party sues or is sued in a representative character the person on whom the estate devolves on the death of the party so suing or sued.

Almost in similar terms is the definition of legal representative under the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 i.e. under Section 2(1)(g).
12.

As observed by this Court in Custodian of Branches of BANCO National Ultramarino vs. Nalini Bai Naique [1989 Supp (2) SCC 275, the definition contained in Section 2(11) CPC is inclusive in character and its scope is wide, it is not confined to legal heirs only.

sentences.text: Instead it stipulates that, a person who may or may not be legal heir competent to inherit the property of the deceased can represent the estate of the deceased person.
It includes heirs as well as persons who represent the estate even without title either as executors or administrators in possession of the estate of the deceased.
All such persons would be covered by the expression "legal representative".

As observed in Gujarat SRTC vs. Ramanbhai Prabhatbhai [(1987) 3 SCC 234 a legal representative is one who suffers on account of death of a person due to a motor vehicle accident and need not necessarily be a Anilkumar G vs Nilesh Navale on 1 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/141366280/

sentences.text: In Manjuri Bera (supra), in paragraph 15 of the said decision, while adverting to the provisions of Section 140 of the Act, the Court observed that even if there is no loss of dependency, the claimant, if he was a legal representative, will be entitled to compensation.
In the concurring judgment of Justice S. H. Kapadia, as His Lordship then was, it is observed that there is distinction between "right to apply for compensation" and "entitlement to compensation".
The compensation constitutes part of the estate of the deceased.
As a result, the legal representative of the deceased would inherit the estate.
Indeed, in that case, the Court was dealing with the case of a married daughter of the deceased and the efficacy of Section 140 of the Act.
Nevertheless, the principle underlying the exposition in this decision would clearly (claimants) even though they are major sons of the deceased and also earning.
14. It is thus settled by now that the legal representatives of the deceased have a right to apply for compensation.

Having said that, it must necessarily follow that even the major married and earning sons of the deceased being legal representatives have a right to apply for compensation and it would be the bounden duty of the Tribunal to consider the application irrespective of the fact whether the concerned legal representative was fully dependent on the deceased and not to limit the claim towards conventional heads only."

20. According to the ratio laid down in above decision, the legal representatives though not fully dependent on the deceased are entitled to claim compensation under all the heads i.e., under both conventional and non-conventional heads.

In order to determine the compensation, the age,
avocation, income, dependency, future prospects of the deceased and other conventional heads are to be ascertained.
21. The compensation towards loss of dependency:
The petitioners No.1 is the father, petitioner No.2 is the mother and petitioner No.3 is the sister of deceased Sandanu A.S.
The petitioners have established that, they are legal representatives of the deceased and they were depending upon the deceased.
Hence, they are entitled to compensation under the head of loss of dependency.
In order to calculate the loss of dependency, the first step is to determine the age and income of the deceased.
i) Age and income of the deceased : The petitioners have averred that, the age of deceased as on the date of accident was 22 years.
To substantiate this point, the petitioners have produced Ex.P.17 Driving Licence of deceased Sandanu A.S., wherein the date of birth of the deceased is mentioned as 07-10-2001.
Admittedly, the accident took place on 30-06-2023.
Therefore, as on the date of accident the age of the deceased was about 22 years.
The petitioners have stated that, as on the date of the accident, the deceased was hale and healthy and was doing business and was earning Rs.30,000/- per month.
Further it is averred that, the deceased was contributing his entire income towards maintaining his family members.
But, it is pertinent to note that, the petitioners have not produced any document to show the deceased Sandanu A.S., was doing business and he was earning Rs.30,000/- per month.

In such circumstances, there is no other option before this Court, except to consider the notional income as income of the deceased as per the guidelines of the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.

Admittedly, in the instant case, as on the date of alleged accident the driver of the offending vehicle bearing Reg. No. MH-12-MV-1905 was not holding valid driving licence to drive the said vehicle.
But, in the present facts and circumstances of the case, the arguments advanced by the learned counsel for petitioners does not hold good.

On the other hand, the arguments advanced by the learned counsel for respondent No.2 holds good and the observations and ratio laid down in the above cited decisions are aptly applicable to case in hand.
Further, no doubt as per the Ex.P.11 charge-sheet, the deceased was not wearing helmet at the time of accident.

But, the evidence on record clearly establishes that, there is no negligence on the part of rider of motorcycle i.e. deceased and the accident has caused on account of sole negligence of the driver of offending vehicle.
As per Ex.P.7 post-mortem report the deceased Sandanu A. S., has not died due to head injury, but due to injuries caused to his major organs.
No doubt, wearing a helmet is crucial for safety.

But, for mere reason that the deceased was not wearing helmet at the time of accident, cannot be sole criteria to hold that, the deceased was equally liable for the cause of accident or to fasten contributory negligence on him, unless his own negligence has contributed to the accident.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
When the accident was not occurred due to the any mechanical defects in the offending vehicle and there was no negligence on the part of motorcycle rider, then it can be presumed that, the said accident had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle.
There is absolutely no rebuttal evidence led by the respondents to disprove the case of the petitioners and even nothing is elicited in the cross-examination of P.W.1 to show that,
the alleged accident has occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the rider of motorcycle i.e.,
deceased and there is no negligence on the part of the driver of Truck bearing Reg. No.
MH-12-MV-1905.
Further, the Ex.P.7 Post-motem report, clearly speaks that, deceased Sandanu A.S., has died due to shock as a result of injury to major organs sustained in the motor vehicle accident.
In such circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the final report filed by the investigation officer and other police records, regarding the negligence of the driver of offending vehicle, place, date and time of accident, involvement of the offending vehicle and injuries caused to deceased Sandanu A.S., in the said accident.
15. Further, it is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims,
the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.
The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011)
SCC 635, has clearly held that, "in a road accident claim cases the strict principle of proof as in a criminal case are not required."
As observed by this Court in Custodian of Branches of BANCO National Ultramarino vs. Nalini Bai Naique [1989 Supp (2) SCC 275, the definition contained in Section 2(11) CPC is inclusive in character and its scope is wide, it is not confined to legal heirs only.
The petitioners have established that, they are legal representatives of the deceased and they were depending upon the deceased.
Hence, they are entitled to compensation under the head of loss of dependency.
In order to calculate the loss of dependency, the first step is to determine the age and income of the deceased.
